'''Sri Lankan Sign Language''' ({{Langx|si|ශ්‍රී ලංකා සංඥා භාෂාව|translit=Śrī Laṁkā Saṁgnā Bhāṣāva}}) is a [[sign language|visual language]] used by [[deaf]] people in [[Sri Lanka]] and has regional variations stemming from the 25 Deaf schools in Sri Lanka.

==Classification==
Wittmann (1991)<ref>{{cite journal |language=fr |last=Wittmann |first=Henri |author-link=Henri Wittmann |year=1991 |title=Classification linguistique des langues signées non vocalement |journal=Revue québécoise de linguistique théorique et appliquée |volume=10 |issue=1 |pages=215–88 |s2cid=162499258 |url=http://www.nou-la.org/ling/1991a-class.pdf}}</ref> posits that the Sri Lankan languages, as a group, are a language isolate ('prototype' sign language), though one developed through [[stimulus diffusion]] from an existing sign language. It is not known if they are related to each other, nor how many there are.
